title: Adjectival Concordance & Elatives
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 11; Ryding Ch. 10)
objectives: Apply fourfold adjectival concordance (gender, number, case, definiteness) between naʿt and manʿūt.
Form comparative clauses using the elative pattern أَفْعَلُ + مِنْ.
Form superlative constructs using أَفْعَلُ in an iḍāfah.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 6: What agreement does an adjective take when modifying a non-human plural noun like الكُتُبُ?

sections.heading: The Fourfold Concordance Rule (Al-Naʿt wa-l-Manʿūt)
sections.body: In Classical Arabic, an attributive adjective (al-naʿt) follows the noun it modifies (al-manʿūt) and agrees with it in four respects: gender, number, grammatical case, and definiteness. (For non-human plurals, the adjective takes feminine singular.)

sections.label: Comparative & Superlative (Ism al-Tafḍīl)
sections.summary: The elative pattern أَفْعَلُ (e.g., أَكْبَرُ 'greater/greatest', أَعْلَمُ 'more/most knowledgeable') is a diptote. Used with مِنْ, it stays masculine singular for comparisons ('greater than'). Placed as muḍāf before an indefinite singular or definite plural, it expresses the superlative ('the greatest of...').

sections.translation: The Qur'an is the greatest book.
sections.irab: القُرْآنُ: مُبْتَدَأٌ مَرْفُوعٌ | أَعْظَمُ: خَبَرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ | كِتَابٍ: مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ مَجْرُورٌ
sections.notes: أَعْظَمُ + indefinite singular genitive (كِتَابٍ) is the standard classical superlative construction ('the greatest of any book' = 'the greatest book').

sections.heading: Color & Defect Adjectives (أَفْعَلُ / فَعْلَاءُ)
sections.body: Adjectives of color and physical traits use أَفْعَلُ for masculine (أَبْيَضُ 'white') and فَعْلَاءُ for feminine (بَيْضَاءُ)—both are diptotes and take no tanwīn.
